pretrain.deduplication: exact text SHA256 before split; same hash cannot cross train/validation

sft.deduplication: canonical conversations SHA256 before split; same hash cannot cross train/validation

model.source: own Dense model initialized from scratch for pretraining

pretrain.scheduler: official cosine schedule, decays to 0.1 * peak LR over all planned optimizer updates
pretrain.attention_backend: forced CUDA FlashAttention; strict right padding and causal self-attention only

sft.scheduler: official cosine schedule, decays to 0.1 * peak LR over all planned optimizer updates
sft.attention_backend: forced CUDA FlashAttention; strict right padding and causal self-attention only
sft.initial_weights: strictly the verified final checkpoint from this experiment's 2-epoch pretraining

checkpoint.retention: keep latest 2 and epoch-boundary checkpoints per stage

explicit_differences_from_official_entry: Official per-step batches are split into micro-batch 4 plus accumulation while preserving effective batches 256 (pretrain) and 16 (SFT).
Pretraining length 340 follows the official entry default; official README recommends approximately 380, so 340 is an explicitly recorded entry-default choice.
Training uses the learner's own Dense ~64M architecture/tokenizer/components, not the upstream model code.
Linux FlashAttention is explicitly forced by a new adapter; the historical hand-written attention and old run identity are not modified.
The local loss normalizes across valid target tokens in the entire accumulated update; this differs from averaging fixed-size upstream microbatch losses when padding varies.
A deterministic deduplicated 1% validation split is reserved from the full pinned source; all other eligible unique records are consumed for both epochs.
not_yet_frozen: full-source audit reports and exact eligible/train/validation counts
